newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer after tame U.S. PPI.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer after tame U.S. PPI.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger in active trade on Thursday, boosted by the release of a report showing U.S. producer prices were subdued in May, analysts said.

"We saw good buying before the (PPI) numbers," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "Because of the lack of supply in the market and the positive tone we have we're really running down."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.86 percent from 2.89 percent at the close of trading on Thursday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened after the U.S. Labor Department reported on Friday that the producer price index fell 0.3 percent in May, compared with expectations of a 0.1 percent rise.
The Canadian money market extended gains made yesterday after the release of a tame U.S. retail sales report reduced expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike rates.

"Usually after we make a run like this people are waiting for a backup as opposed to coming back in and buying more, but we continue to see the same accounts back in continuing to add to their long positions," said the trader.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.06 percent from 3.14 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.60 percent from 3.70 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 2.95 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
